why: Provenance + behaviour contract for the image this recipe serves. The image is ALSO patched at runtime by the bootstrap (the valid_object shim), so a manifest digest alone does not prove what is running: the build stamp and the engine-critical file hashes do. A NEW upstream nightly will FAIL this gate until it is re-audited -- that is the intended adoption gate, not a bug.
files_note: Every file that EMITS a log marker or a metric label the post-boot verifier asserts is pinned here. Without that, a fork that changed a log format could make the verifier pass on a string it invented, or fail for a reason that has nothing to do with the behaviour. The pins below the flashinfer loader are the marker sources: vllm/config/scheduler.py (the chunked-prefill boundary), vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py (the block-size LCM), vllm/v1/metrics/loggers.py (the cache_config_info metric family), vllm/model_executor/kernels/linear/__init__.py (the dense MXFP8 kernel choice), vllm/v1/engine/core.py and vllm/config/vllm.py (the startup config dump), vllm/model_executor/models/config.py (the TP=3 head padding), vllm/config/model.py (the parallel-config check whose TP=3 relaxation the fork carries), vllm/config/cache.py (the DS-V4.1 block-size constants). The attention-backend marker is read from a line the b12x readiness reporter prints, so two more files decide what that line says and are pinned with it: flashinfer/experimental/b12x/preparation/_progress.py (the readiness line's format) and flashinfer/experimental/b12x/_api.py (the static logical-op registry that supplies the 'attention.dsa_indexer' name in it). The all-reduce transport marker is read from the engine's own dispatch line, so its emitter is pinned too: vllm/distributed/device_communicators/cuda_communicator.py. The FORBIDDEN markers are asserted on absence, so their emitters are pinned for the same reason: vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/oracle/mxfp4.py (the 'B12X_MXFP4' MoE enum name) and vllm/model_executor/layers/fused_moe/oracle/nvfp4.py (the 'NvFp4 MoE backend' message) — a fork that reworded either message would otherwise make a forbidden check pass on a string it no longer emits. THE INDEXER FAMILY IS PINNED FOR ITS OWN SAKE: the DSA indexer's top-k selection is the one place where this model can return plausible-but-wrong output with no error signal. Upstream documents the default selection as breaking ties by thread scheduling (https://vllm.ai/blog/2026-10-14-train-inference-consistency), and the fix would have to be a RECIPE-SIDE patch — none is shipped here — not an upstream merge — so the bytes that decide the tie are exactly the bytes worth pinning. OVERLAY NOTE: vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py and vllm/v1/kv_cache_interface.py are pinned at the capacity-overlay bytes (the steady/transient split, class of open upstream PR vllm-project/vllm#52495); the bootstrap installs them from /kit/overlay before this gate runs, so a drifted or absent overlay fails here loudly.

semantic.flashinfer/experimental/b12x/preparation: valid_object must be resolvable (from b12x._lib.cache_integrity) OR the bootstrap shim must be present — the bootstrap may patch this file in-container, so its hash is deliberately NOT pinned

model_contract.why: Facts about the MODEL that the engine reads and that a silent numerical error would hide. The code that consumes them is hash-pinned under `files`; these values pin the inputs.
model_contract.text_config.swiglu_limit.why: The clamped-SwiGLU limit for the routed experts. The chain is: model config -> DeepseekV41Config.swiglu_limit -> the inherited DeepseekV4 MoE class -> RoutedExperts.swiglu_limit -> the MXFP4 quant method -> gemm1_clamp_limit -> the kernel's clamp_limit. If any link stops carrying it, every decode step silently uses unclamped SwiGLU with no error signal.

resolved_backends.why: What the engine RESOLVES, which is not the same as the flags the recipe passes: the dense-linear kernel and the attention backend are selected by the engine's own policy — and the MoE backend's resolution still has to be proven even though the launcher pins it — and a rebase can change what the recipe's command line resolves. The code that resolves them is hash-pinned under `files`; these are the values that resolution must produce. Checked by verify-resolved-backends.py after the engine is up.

expect.why.moe_backend: The b12x MXFP4 MoE backend, measured and kept: ~31 tok/s solo decode, clean 4-stream parity, prefill in band, trough ~2.8 GB.
expect.why.attention_backend: The b12x attention kernels are the ones that run: the DSA indexer and the compressed-sparse MLA kernels are compiled and primed by the b12x autotuner at warmup. The marker is value-bearing, so a different attention backend cannot pass it by accident.
expect.why.tp3_head_pad: The fork's TP=3 head surgery, applied at engine-config time. Upstream vLLM refuses TP=3 for this model (64 attention heads do not divide by 3); the fork pads to 72 heads in 9 output groups instead. This marker proves the surgery is live, and it is emitted by a file the manifest hash-pins.
expect.why.scheduler_block_size: The requested block size; the engine logs the LCM of the KV groups' block sizes.
expect.why.requested_block_size: What the command line ASKED for, read from the container's own argv. The LCM is what the engine resolved and the metric label is the minimum across the KV groups; neither proves the flag was actually forwarded. This is the check that closes that gap.
expect.why.reported_block_size: What /metrics reports for cache_config_info.block_size: the MINIMUM across the prefix-cacheable KV groups, not the requested value. DS-V4.1's sliding-window group is 128, so a 256 request reports 128. Both are asserted because a reader checking only one of them is misled.
expect.why.enable_prefix_caching: On by default in this build, so the sliding-window replay path is live on a request that hits the cache. The long-prompt gate checks that a cache hit does not change the decode logprobs.
expect.why.sliding_window: DS-V4.1's sliding-window size; 128 is what puts the sliding-window group on the 128 block size.
expect.why.max_num_batched_tokens: The chunked-prefill boundary. The long-prompt correctness gate builds a prompt that crosses it, because upstream vLLM #62811 shows the failure lives in the LAST chunk of a chunked prefill when it runs as a piecewise CUDA graph -- a short prompt never reaches it.
expect.why.allreduce_backend: WHICH ALL-REDUCE ACTUALLY ENGAGED. The recipe sets VLLM_ENABLE_ROCE_ALLREDUCE=1 and VLLM_ROCE_ALLREDUCE_MAX_SIZE=2MB, and the image ships a one-shot RoCE collective (B12X_ROCENANTE) that needs BOTH RoCE rails of every link to reach the peer. The shipped topology is one cable per PAIR OF BOXES -- three cables, each device connected to the other two, both of each device's ports in use -- so on that topology the collective cannot form, the engine falls through, and PYNCCL carries the reduction -- and the recipe would otherwise say nothing about it. Pinning the EXPECTED value turns a silent fallback into a check: a reader who adds a second cable between the same pair of boxes gets a FAIL here until they update this expectation to B12X_ROCENANTE, which is the point -- the fabric change is then a gated event rather than an unrecorded one. The engine prints the choice as "Using ['<backend>'] all-reduce backends (in dispatch order) for group 'tp:0' out of potential backends: [...]".
expect.why.tiny_decode_env: B12X_W4A8_TINY_DECODE=0 disables the b12x tiny-decode path whose small-batch SwiGLU drops the clamp; with it off, the general kernel receives the clamp through plan_weights. This env is the binding clamp check now that b12x is the expected backend.

forbidden.nvfp4_moe_backend.why: The CUTLASS NVFP4 MoE path finalises expert outputs with atomics, so identical requests give different logits on this hardware. It is not the backend this recipe selects.
